surprises.description: Core EPS was $3.50, $0.35 (about 11%) above the $3.15 consensus estimate. That was a meaningful upside beat, though slightly below the preview’s bull-case range of $3.55–$3.75.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 core earnings were $956 million, or $3.50 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus calls for Q3 core EPS of $3.15.”

surprises.description: Catastrophe losses came in far above the preview’s expected benign, sub-consensus cat load: they were $198 million, or 4.2 points. The preview’s consensus bridge implied only about 3.1 points for cats and prior-year development combined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Catastrophe losses rose sharply to $198 million (4.2 points).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Benign backdrop should deliver a sub-consensus cat number”; consensus BI reported CR of 92.6% versus underlying 89.5% implied “+3.1 points of cat and prior-year development.”

surprises.description: Middle & Large deteriorated instead of delivering the preview’s expected improvement: its combined ratio was 99.5%, with higher non-CAT property and workers’ compensation losses. The accompanying broad-based workers’ comp frequency uptick added about 1 point to the all-in BI combined ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle & Large deteriorated to a 99.5% combined ratio from higher non-CAT property and workers' comp losses”; workers’ compensation had “a broad-based uptick in claim frequency, adding about 1 point to the all-in BI combined ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 guide was for “middle & large underlying CR roughly a point better than the 93.3 YTD level in 2H,” conditional on non-cat property normalizing.

surprises.description: Business Insurance’s underlying combined ratio was 90.1%, 0.6 points worse than the 89.5% consensus estimate. This is consistent with the underwriting pressures appearing in Middle & Large and workers’ compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Insurance grew written premium 6% with a 90.1% underlying combined ratio.”

surprises.description: Business Insurance renewal pricing excluding workers’ compensation declined by 40 basis points to 5.3%, indicating greater price competition than the preview had quantified, despite its warning about increasing competition in Middle & Large.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Insurance renewal written pricing excluding workers' comp declined 40 basis points to 5.3%, signaling an increasingly competitive and softening commercial market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “increasing competition in the middle and large space,” particularly GL and workers’ comp.

surprises.description: Small Business new business turned non-positive for the first time in roughly 20-plus quarters amid rising competition. The preview discussed competition in Middle & Large but did not flag this deterioration in Small Business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Small Business delivered an exceptional 85.2% underlying combined ratio … with 7% premium growth, though new business turned non-positive for the first time in roughly 20+ quarters amid rising competition.”

surprises.description: Investment income and limited-partnership returns were stronger than the preview’s expectations: NII rose 13% year over year and LP returns were 10.2% annualized, above the prior 7.6% annualized pace and the expectation that second-half returns would be generally consistent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net investment income rose 13% year-over-year to $850 million, aided by strong 10.2% annualized limited partnership returns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 NII was “$800mm, +22% YoY, with LP returns at 7.6% annualized in 1H and guidance for 2H ‘generally consistent’”; consensus P&C NII was “$633.9mm” (+4.8%).

surprises.description: The Equitable Employee Benefits acquisition is expected to modestly dilute 2027 core earnings, including about $30 million of annual intangible amortization. The preview did not identify this acquisition or flag this dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recently closed Equitable Employee Benefits acquisition adds ~$500 million in annual premium but will be modestly dilutive to 2027 core earnings, including ~$30 million of annual intangible amortization.”

surprises.description: The company announced a 12% dividend increase to $0.67 per share effective January 2027, an unanticipated capital-return announcement in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its common quarterly dividend by 12% to $0.67 per share effective January 2027.”
